newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC plans organisational reform.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC plans organisational reform.

text.p: India's Oil and Natural Gas Corp is refurbishing its organisation to introduce a multi-disciplinary asset management approach, ONGC chairman B.C. Bora said.

"Instead of the compartmental business group concept, each of the areas will be headed by an asset manager empowered to decide on investment, exploration, development and production," Bora said in an interview late on Thursday.

"The bulk of the decision making in that area will lie with the managers and only in a few cases will they require our approval. Different parameters will be set for different fields on the basis of which performance of the asset managers will be assessed."
Initially the profit-centre concept will be introduced in the producing basins of Bombay Offshore, Assam and Cambay for enhancing oil recovery, Bora said.
A task force has been set up to identify the fields which will be taken up as pilot projects. "The concept in the three oilfields should be in place in a month's time," he said.
"If they show results, we can roll out the same thing for the entire organisation.

Bora said the concept has been recommended by consultants McKinsey & Co which also suggested hiving off ONGC's different activities of drilling, sesmic survey and data-logging, among others, into service subsidiaries.

"As a first step, we will be setting up an offshore drilling outfit with two rigs for hiring out services to other companies," Bora said. The ONGC is bidding for drilling in Bangladesh and Yemen as well as for exploration companies operating in India, he said.
If successful, the drilling outfit will be converted into a wholly-owned subsidiary, Bora said.
